content.text:
The fix is complete. 

## Summary

The bug: when a test class inherited from multiple base classes each carrying different pytest markers, only one class's markers survived because `pytestmark` is a plain attribute resolved by normal attribute lookup (which returns the first match in MRO).

The fix in `src/_pytest/mark/structures.py`:

1. **`get_unpacked_marks`** now, for classes, walks the full MRO (`obj.__mro__` in reverse order) reading each class's *own* `pytestmark` (via `__dict__`, not inherited attribute lookup) and concatenates them. Non-class objects keep the original behavior. This merges markers from all base classes instead of losing some.

2. **`store_mark`** now calls `get_unpacked_marks(obj, consider_mro=False)` so that when a marker is applied to a class, only that class's own directly-applied marks are read back — preventing parent-class marks from being physically copied onto the child (which would cause duplicates).

Verified both `foo` and `bar` marks now appear on `TestDings`, and the existing mark/skipping/collection test suites still pass.
